expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Williams sits at 9.5% projected ownership and the reason is structural rather than performance-related: Chicago is difficult to stack. No pass catcher has cleared a 19% target share in his six starts, four different players have led the team in targets across those games, and the projections have Burden, Loveland and Odunze within half a target of one another. That ambiguity is what keeps the field away, and it’s the wrong reason to pass on the quarterback. This is a Ben Johnson offense running more plays than anyone in football at 69.3 a game and scoring 26.8 points, home off a bye as an 11.5-point favorite in a 48.5-point game — an implied 30 — against a New Orleans defense allowing 26.2 points a contest that ranks 24th in sacks and has forced four interceptions all year. Exposure to that offense is worth accepting the uncertainty at the receiving spot. Loveland is my preferred partner: he’s led the team in targets twice, carries the highest projected target count on the roster at $5,100, and his 26.9 ceiling sits within range of Burden’s for $1,200 less.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: Caleb Williams has one of the highest ceilings of any QB on the slate, and his ownership should stay in check with the field gravitating heavily to the TEN/DAL game, and the Bears can name their score here.

players.notes: Highest pass volume in a 30-point implied total against a weak secondary.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: The Titans have allowed three straight 300-yard passing performances, with Joe Burrow throwing six TDs, Trevor Lawrence adding three, and Watson contributing a rushing TD. The WR production has been just as ridiculous. Tee Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase combined for 21 receptions, 296 yards, and three TDs. Parker Washington had 148 receiving yards in one half, while Josh Cameron added three catches for 67 yards and a TD. Zay Flowers finished with eight receptions for 118 yards and a TD, and DeVonta Smith posted 10 catches for 117 yards and a score.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: Dak gets an incredible matchup against the Titans who continue to give up huge games to opposing QB’s and WR’s.  Last week we saw Dak and company explode and this matchup is even better and we know where the WR production is going - straight to CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.  The Titans have been torched by receivers all season long and I will be looking to build around Dak/CeeDee/ and Pickens this week.

players.notes: Elite pass volume in the highest game total on the slate at 54.5 points.
Strong passing floor with a massive 15.5-point home favorite spread.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: Don't look now, but that's back-to-back games with multiple touchdown passes for Cam Ward, and they've come against two fairly good defenses, especially Jacksonville last week. The Titans have made a concerted effort recently to fully turn the keys over to Ward and see if he really is a starting quarterback in the NFL. This week, he gets his most generous matchup of the season against the gift that keeps on giving: the Dallas defense.

players.notes: Multiple touchdown passes in back-to-back games facing the Dallas defense.
Solid passing metrics in a tight divisional matchup with a 42.5 total.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text:
This is mainly a DK play at the price point.

McCarthy has averaged over eight yards per attempt in three of four games with the Giants and over nine yards per attempt against zone coverage. I’m buying into that efficiency at a discounted price in a game where New York should be trailing. Isaiah Likely is my preferred stacking option, as he’s been McCarthy’s primary target against zone coverage all season. Jacksonville hasn’t faced a TE of Likely’s caliber, and with the Jaguars playing so much zone, I think this duo has massive upside at their price points.

players.notes: High efficiency against zone coverage while trailing in a 46.5 game total.
Strong passing volume expected while trailing in a high 48.5 game total.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Tampa’s standing against quarterbacks is built almost entirely on takeaways. They lead the league with 16 interceptions in nine games while ranking 27th in sacks and ninth in passing yards allowed, so the suppression is coming from turnovers rather than pressure — and interception rate is the least repeatable thing a defense does. The schedule has flattered them as well: four of those starts came against Bryce Young, Michael Penix, Caleb Williams and Deshaun Watson, and the two performances anchoring the season line were four-interception afternoons from Penix and Williams. Goff has thrown multiple touchdowns in six of nine games and did not turn the ball over once through his first six starts. At $6,100 with 7% projected ownership, home and favored, the market is reading this matchup off the picks and I’ll take the other side.

players.notes: Multiple passing touchdowns in six of nine games as a home favorite.
Strong passing floor as a home favorite in a 46.5-point game total.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: I'd love to galaxy brain a fade position for someone this popular, but Emmett projects for nearly the most fantasy points of any player on the entire slate at bargain prices.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: I will be locking Emmett Johnson in on every lineup I make even though his ownerships is projected to be much higher this week than it was last week.  He gets another elite matchup and he easily could be the highest scoring player on the slate with all of the opportunities he gets in the Chiefs offense.  I’m locking him in and moving on.

players.notes: Elite rushing volume and goal-line work for a heavy home favorite.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: Pollard has three straight games as a top-3 RB in PPR and now has the highest Titans team total of the year against his former team

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: Pollard is my favorite bring back option in my Dallas stacks as this is the highest total game on the slate and Pollard is now 12th overall in the NFL for rushing yards at 628.  The Cowboys are allowing the most rushing yards per game at 154 and we have seen Pollard explode the last few weeks as he has had 5 rushing TD’s and 1 receiving TD in the last three games alone.

players.notes: Top-tier rushing workload facing the worst run defense in the league.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: Coleman has taken over the Broncos’ backfield, playing over 65% of the snaps in two straight games while seeing at least 15 touches in both. Now he gets a Raiders defense that has been one of the worst in football against RBs this season. With his recent workload and a matchup this favorable, I think Coleman is in a great spot to have a massive game.

players.notes: Workhorse backfield role with over 65 percent snap share and 15 touches.
Elite explosive run and catch role as a home favorite against Tampa.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: You're typically not going to get much going in the run game against a defense like San Francisco, but the volume for Williams, even in that matchup, was very encouraging. Dallas is still dealing with injuries at running back, and he's borderline the only guy they feel comfortable giving carries to right now. There's a chance the game script is very favorable for Williams, which could lead to one of those ceiling games.

players.notes: Heavy rushing volume and goal-line work with a highly favorable game script.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: The Lions run defense allows greater than 5 YPC without Aidan Hutchinson, and they also do not have linebacker Jack Campbell. Bucky has been the entire Bucs offense, as they lean on the run and their defense, and the Lions new run defense might be extremely exploitable.

players.notes: Solid rushing share and pass-catching involvement in a 46.5 game total.
Valuable rushing touches and goal-line potential in a tight divisional game.
Primary rushing workhorse with elite goal-line upside as a road underdog.
Strong rushing volume and snap share as a home favorite against Baltimore.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: On FanDuel, I'm hunting touchdowns from running backs, and this is a solid matchup for Chicago. There's no running back in the league these days who has as much three-touchdown upside as DeAndre Swift.

expert_blurbs.author: NeilCO
expert_blurbs.text: Kyle Monangai is expected to return for this game, which could cut into Swift's highest potential ceiling. But it's also drastically cutting into his pOWN%, and Swift has shown that he can excel with Monangai active. Swift has averaged 16.38 fantasy points per game even with Monangai this year. In an elite matchup, and with Monangai potentially seeing limited action in his first game back, Swift is a great tournament play.

players.notes: Explosive multi-touchdown upside as a primary weapon in a high team total.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: Burden is the top pass game target for a team that can hang a HUGE number against the woeful Saints defense. He has put up big scores even against tough defenses like Seattle and Tampa Bay, and he's not priced to the level of the other elite fantasy WRs on the slate, nor is he going to be popular.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: Luther Burden has had a touchdown in each of the last three games putting him over 640 receiving yards on the season along with 4 total TD’s.  He is a huge focal point of this offense and I want to make sure I have a piece of this Bears offense in each of my lineups with the Bears having the 3rd highest implied total on the slate this week.  Luther Burden, Colston Loveland, and D’Andre Swift are all elite options to mix in and I will have exposure to each of them along with their QB, Caleb Williams.

players.notes: Top target share in a high-scoring offense facing a weak secondary.
Elite target volume and route participation in the highest game total.
Strong route participation and deep threat role in a 54.5 game total.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: This is a DraftKings play for me because of the PPR format. If the Saints continue to use Tyson like they did last week, with all those short passes around the line of scrimmage, then he's best suited for this format, and the price is right.

players.notes: Frequent short-area targets in the slot for full-point PPR formats.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Tennessee has allowed more DraftKings points to wide receivers than any defense in football at 42.2 a game, which makes this the best receiving matchup on the board, and the field is going to buy into it through CeeDee Lamb. Lamb projects for 30.6% ownership at $8,800; Pickens comes in at 22% and $6,800. That gap is the opportunity, because the target hierarchy is less settled than the pricing suggests — Pickens out-targeted Lamb 19 to 13 last week on the way to 145 yards and three scores, and he has averaged 10 targets over his last four. Two thousand dollars cheaper, in the same offense, against the same defense, with a comparable path to a 30-point ceiling, he’s the better way to attack this game.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: We saw Pickens explode last week going for 145 yards with 11 catches and 3 total TD’s against the 49ers.  He now gets an even better game environment carrying the highest total on the slate at 55 and Pickens is still priced in that mid-tier on both sites.  We know where the targets are going in this offense so I am going right back to the well playing both CeeDee Lamb and Pickens, even though they are both going to be popular.

players.notes: Led the team with 19 targets and 145 yards against the league's worst secondary.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: The same Tampa profile that suppresses quarterbacks has not translated to wide receivers. They rank 21st in DraftKings points allowed to the position and 13th in targets faced, which is to say ordinary, and the interceptions driving their reputation don’t take targets away from a slot receiver seeing double digits every week. St. Brown remains the most dependable volume at the position in football: 10.1 targets a game, a 28% share of Detroit’s attempts, and seven touchdowns in nine games. His last outing was five targets for 98 yards and two scores, which is the point — the touchdown equity holds even when the target count dips. At $8,200 and 16.5% projected ownership he is not a leverage play, but he is the best receiver in a game the market is avoiding for the wrong reason.

players.notes: Elite target floor with a 28 percent target share and high catch volume.
Primary perimeter target expected to see high route participation.
Strong slot route rate and target volume in a trailing game script.
Deep threat role with high air yards share in a high-scoring matchup.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: The Jaguars have one of the single best run defenses in the entire leauge, which forces opponents to the air. They have smothered opposing TEs to this point of the season, which means we could see even more of the targets go to Nabers in this one (and a few less to Isaiah Likely). With some strong value RBs, we have the salary to fit Nabers in this pass funnel matchup, and he's already earned a 30% target share and 35% air yards share, both tops on the Giants.

players.notes: A 30 percent target share and 35 percent air yards share in a pass funnel.
Strong route participation and explosive yards after catch potential.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Loveland is the highest-projected tight end on the main slate at $5,100 and still only 11.7% owned. The usage has turned sharply: nine targets a game over his last three, including a 33% share in one of them, and he has led Chicago in targets twice this season. New Orleans has been the seventh-most generous defense to the position. He is also the cleanest way into Williams in an offense where the receiving room is a coin flip week to week — the quarterback is 9.5% owned and the tight end is 11.7%, and the pair costs less than most single stacking pieces on this slate. I think he’s the best tight end play on the board.

players.notes: A surge to nine targets per game over his last three outings.
Primary tight end target against zone coverage in a pass-leaning script.
Reliable seam and red-zone targets in a close divisional game.
Solid route rate and red-zone involvement in a high total matchup.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Detroit has allowed more DraftKings points to tight ends than any defense in football at 22.9 a game and has surrendered 11 touchdowns to the position, also the most in the league. That is the single best positional matchup available this week and it costs $3,300. The honest problem is that Otton has not been part of the offense lately — 3.7 targets a game over his last three and a 14% share on the season. He is a punt rather than a play, and the case is simply that the cost is almost nothing while the matchup carries real touchdown equity in a game where Tampa is likely throwing from behind. At 5.8% ownership I’ll take the shot in large-field builds and leave him out of everything smaller.

players.notes: Facing a defense allowing the most points and touchdowns to tight ends.
Elite target share and route participation as a primary offensive weapon.
Consistent route participation and red-zone role as a massive favorite.
Elite target earner with unmatched route participation at the position.
Strong route rate and red-zone role in a high-paced game environment.
